verdict.rationale: Ledgy offers per-integration service accounts, created under Company Settings, that authenticate via the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. The docs describe these credentials as scoped per integration, short-lived and immediately revocable, so a company could hand a separate non-admin credential to a third party. In-app permission segmentation and access control over reporting also exist, but nothing documents a delegated third-party authorization flow or how finely data can be scoped. Missing for 10: a delegated/consent-based third-party access flow (e.g. OAuth authorization code for partner apps), documented field- or data-slice-level scopes for API credentials, explicit support for external parties such as law firms or wealth managers, and independent corroboration.
